title: Codonopsis pilosula polysaccharides alleviate neuronal apoptosis induced by endoplasmic reticulum stress-activated PERK-ATF4-CHOP signaling in APP/PS1 mice.
authors: Cai, Yuanqin; Wang, Xi; Xiang, Yang; Wang, Zhenning; Long, Qinghua; Zeng, Chuhua
one_liner_zh: 研究党参多糖通过PERK-ATF4-CHOP通路缓解AD小鼠神经元凋亡，仅含分子对接但非蛋白-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: BackgroundCodonopsis polysaccharides (CPPs) shows neuroprotective potential in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and may reduce neuronal apoptosis by modulating endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS).ObjectiveTo investigate the protective mechanisms of CPPs against neuronal apoptosis in APP/PS1 mice, focusing on the ERS response and the PERK-ATF4-CHOP signaling pathway.MethodsAPP/PS1 mice were orally administered CPPs at different doses. Their learning and memory abilities were evaluated using the Morris water maze (MWM). The integrity of hippocampal neurons and senile plaque deposition were assessed using histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence. The expression of amyloid-beta (Abeta) plaques secretase protein, ERS markers, and apoptosis-related proteins was assessed using western blot analyses. The affinity of the PERK-ATF4-CHOP pathway and CPPs was analyzed and assessed using molecular docking.ResultsMWM testing revealed that CPPs improved the learning and memory abilities of APP/PS1 mice. Histopathological examination confirmed that CPPs reduced hippocampal neuronal apoptosis. Immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence analysis showed that CPPs decreased Abeta protein expression and ERS. Western blot analysis further confirmed that CPPs reduced the expression of proteins related to Abeta synthesis; downregulated the expression of glucose-regulated protein 78 (GRP78), PERK, ATF4, CHOP, and Bcl-2 associated X protein (Bax), while upregulating the expression of B-cell lymphoma 2 (Bcl-2).ConclusionsThis study demonstrates that CPPs exert neuroprotective effects by targeting the PERK-ATF4-CHOP signaling pathway and alleviating ERS, suggesting a novel approach and potential therapeutic agent for AD treatment.
abstract_zh: 背景：党参多糖（CPPs）在阿尔茨海默病（AD）中显示出神经保护潜力，并可能通过调节内质网应激（ERS）减少神经元凋亡。目的：探讨CPPs对APP/PS1小鼠神经元凋亡的保护机制，重点关注ERS反应及PERK-ATF4-CHOP信号通路。方法：对APP/PS1小鼠口服不同剂量的CPPs。使用Morris水迷宫（MWM）评估其学习记忆能力。通过组织病理学、免疫组织化学和免疫荧光评估海马神经元的完整性和老年斑沉积。使用western blot分析评估淀粉样蛋白-β（Abeta）斑块分泌酶蛋白、ERS标志物及凋亡相关蛋白的表达。通过分子对接分析并评估PERK-ATF4-CHOP通路与CPPs的亲和力。结果：MWM测试显示，CPPs改善了APP/PS1小鼠的学习记忆能力。组织病理学检查证实，CPPs减少了海马神经元凋亡。免疫组织化学和免疫荧光分析显示，CPPs降低了Abeta蛋白表达和ERS。Western blot分析进一步证实，CPPs降低了与Abeta合成相关蛋白的表达；下调了葡萄糖调节蛋白78（GRP78）、PERK、ATF4、CHOP和Bcl-2相关X蛋白（Bax）的表达，同时上调了B细胞淋巴瘤2（Bcl-2）的表达。结论：本研究证明，CPPs通过靶向PERK-ATF4-CHOP信号通路并缓解ERS发挥神经保护作用，为AD治疗提供了一种新方法和潜在治疗药物。
